transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Nexora), Dana Liu (Nexora), Carlos Mendes (Nexora)
Link: https://redwood.ai/decks/dedicated-nexora.pdf

Summary: Brief discovery focused on reserved GPUs, tenant isolation, burst/prewarm strategy, and security/compliance gating for a pilot. Nexora is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; leaning Dedicated if isolation & predictable latency are met.

Topics: reserved capacity, warm pool/prewarm, tenant fencing, VPC & KMS, SOC 2, expected QPS and burst envelope, fallback to hosted variants

[00:00] Alex Rivera: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Alex, I'm the AE on this.
[00:12] Samir Patel: Thanks Alex, yeah appreciate it. Quick note, we're on a tight timeline — pilot by end of July would be ideal.
[00:18] Priya Kapoor: Hi all, Priya here, I'm the solutions engineer. Today I'd love to map out your burst envelope and isolation needs so we can see if Redwood Dedicated fits.
[00:27] Dana Liu: Cool, I'll start with context: Nexora runs inference for clinical summarization and triage. Typical latency target is sub-150ms p50 on short prompts, but some flows tolerate up to 500ms p95. We have nightly batch jobs and daytime spikes around reports release.
[00:44] Carlos Mendes: Also data residency matters — US-east for now but may need EU later. We're evaluating both Dedicated and a VPC private deployment.
[00:52] Alex Rivera: Got it; when you say spikes, what's the delta between baseline and peak?
[01:03] Samir Patel: Our baseline is pretty low, like 30 qps, but during batch releases and some product events we've seen 600-800 qps for short windows, 5–12 minutes. We call that our "blip" traffic.
[01:15] Priya Kapoor: That's helpful. Do you have concurrency per request (token length) distributions? Short prompts vs long?
[01:22] Dana Liu: Short prompts are 16-64 tokens mostly; long ones are 512+ for summaries. The blast traffic is usually the short prompts.
[01:30] Alex Rivera: Ok so we should think about a mixed profile: dedicated pool sized for your steady throughput with headroom and a warm pool for bursts.
[01:38] [00:01:45] Samir Patel: Question: how does Redwood handle isolation? We can't have cross-tenant noisy neighbors for clinical data, and we need audit logs.
[01:47] Priya Kapoor: Right. For Dedicated we can provide tenant isolation at node level — reserved GPU nodes that only host your workloads. We also have VPC Private if you need customer-managed network. There is also a mixed mode where control plane is Redwood-hosted but inference runs on dedicated hardware bound to your account.
[02:05] Carlos Mendes: Is it single-tenant hardware or virtualized containers on shared nodes?
[02:11] Priya Kapoor: Single-tenant in the sense that the GPU instances are reserved for you — so no other customers share those physical GPUs. The orchestration still uses our runtime, but it's logically fenced. There are trade-offs with elasticity and cost.
[02:26] Alex Rivera: I'll flag the SLA for isolation and an excerpt from the contract — same for audit logs. We'll include that in the deck.
[02:34] [00:03:10] Dana Liu: How about burst? If we have 800 qps spikes, do you do autoscaling instantly or is there prewarm we need to configure?
[02:43] Priya Kapoor: We have a combination — autoscale for steady growth and warm pools for sudden spikes. Warm pools prewarm model kernels and KV cache state so cold-start overhead is reduced. Prewarming takes time depending on model size — for 70B-ish models think multiple minutes unless prewarmed/resident.
[02:57] Samir Patel: Hmm, multiples minutes might be too slow for a 5–12 minute blip.
[03:05] Priya Kapoor: That's why we size the warm pool and have hot standby nodes — you can configure a hotpool for your account that keeps N prewarmed replicas. There's cost to keep them warm, but it's the usual latency vs cost tradeoff.
[03:18] Alex Rivera: To make it concrete: we can propose a baseline of X reserved GPUs to cover your 30 qps steady state, plus a hotpool that covers up to 800 qps for short bursts. We'll run a cost model.
[03:29] [00:04:00] Samir Patel: Also, if those hotpool nodes are reserved, do we still get the data isolation guarantees?
[03:35] Priya Kapoor: Yep — hotpool nodes are still part of your dedicated reservation. They won't host other tenants.
[03:41] Dana Liu: Ok good. On encryption and keys: we need customer-managed KMS and HSM support for model artifacts and request logs.
[03:50] Priya Kapoor: We support KMS integrations — for Private we can do HSM. For Dedicated we can integrate with your cloud KMS (bring-your-own-keys) for key wrapping. We'll add that to the security deep dive.
[03:59] [00:05:00] Carlos Mendes: SOC 2 is a requirement; do you have SOC 2 Type II? Also SSO/SAML for RBAC.
[04:08] Alex Rivera: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II, ISO is in progress — I can share the certs. We support SAML and SCIM for provisioning and fine-grained RBAC in Console. We'll attach the compliance pack.
[04:18] Samir Patel: Another operational question: in the event of capacity constraints, what's the fallback? We can't fail our triage flow.
[04:27] Priya Kapoor: Several options: route to a smaller model variant (cheaper and less memory) within your Dedicated pool, fallback to Redwood-hosted compatible endpoint (if you allow it), or queue requests with graceful degradation. We can define an A/B policy; Redwood's smart routing can favor latency or cost.
[04:43] Dana Liu: Are model quantized variants supported? We have some quantized checkpoints we want to serve.
[04:48] Priya Kapoor: Yes — quantized models supported on certain instance types. We'll check compatibility with your model family. Some optimizations affect latency/quality so we'll recommend evals.
[04:59] [00:06:30] Alex Rivera: Quick logistics: for benchmarking, could you send a 48-hour sample with a mix of short and long prompts, and the token distribution? We can run an internal benchmark against a dedicated pool and report latency, throughput, and cost.
[05:08] Samir Patel: Yes we can. We'll sanitize a sample and send it. We'll aim to get it by Monday.
[05:15] Carlos Mendes: On networking, we need VPC peering and private endpoints for the inference nodes. Any outbound calls from nodes?
[05:24] Priya Kapoor: Nodes don't phone home with raw payloads; control plane telemetry is minimal and can be routed via private links in VPC mode. We'll detail the egress profile.
[05:33] Dana Liu: Great. Also, billing model: is dedicated capacity flat monthly commitment? Do you support burst credits?
[05:41] Alex Rivera: Dedicated is typically a monthly reserved commit with optional burst credits for short-term overage. We can structure a pilot with a small commit + burst allowance. We'll include pricing tiers in the deck.
[05:52] [00:08:00] Samir Patel: Ok, if we agree to dedicated for pilot, what is the on-ramp time — how long to provision reserved GPUs and prewarm?
[06:01] Priya Kapoor: Provisioning reserved capacity is usually 3–7 business days once contracts are signed and payment details are processed. Prewarm depends on model size and how many replicas you want prewarmed — a day or two to fully validate. If you need sub-24hr, we can try a fast ramp with higher burst credits but it's not guaranteed.
[06:18] Carlos Mendes: That aligns with our July pilot target but we'll need security review earlier.
[06:24] Alex Rivera: We'll prioritize the security pack to unblock that.
[06:28] [00:09:15] Dana Liu: Are there any limitations with KV cache or context window size on prewarmed nodes? We rely on long context for summarization.
[06:36] Priya Kapoor: The runtime supports large context windows up to 64k in certain model families; there are memory tradeoffs. Prewarm helps with KV cache population for repeated prefixes but very long context can still increase per-token latency. We'll capture your longest context examples in the benchmark.
[06:52] Samir Patel: Regarding monitoring: we need token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency dashboards — can we get per-tenant telemetry and traces?
[07:01] Priya Kapoor: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, per-model breakdowns, per-route SLOs, and tracing hooks. For Dedicated we can also ship logs to your SIEM.
[07:11] [00:10:30] Alex Rivera: I'm going to log two follow ups: 1) Security deep dive with our security PM + your security team, 2) Benchmark kickoff once sample is uploaded.
[07:20] Samir Patel: Makes sense. One more trick question — preemption: if hardware is preemptible or scheduled maintenance occurs, what's the behavior?
[07:29] Priya Kapoor: For Dedicated we provision on non-preemptible hardware as default. For cost-optimized tiers sometimes preemptible is offered with explicit fallback to hosted. We'll avoid preemptible for clinical workloads.
[07:40] Carlos Mendes: Good. Also want to call out SLA targets: p50 and p95 latency goals and uptime for Dedicated.
[07:48] Alex Rivera: We'll provide the SLA excerpt in the deck, including uptime SLA and latency objectives for reserved pools.
[07:55] [00:12:00] Dana Liu: Any red flags you see with our plan? We're fairly conservative — security is a gating factor.
[08:03] Priya Kapoor: Nothing major. Main items are: sizing warmpool appropriately, prewarming for short blips, and confirming KMS/HSM needs. Also decide whether the control plane being Redwood-hosted is acceptable — some customers require fully private control plane (we support Private deployments but it's heavier).
[08:20] Samir Patel: We probably prefer Redwood-managed control plane for speed unless compliance pushes us to private. We'll decide after the security review.
[08:28] Alex Rivera: Great. We'll send the deck and the isolation SLA excerpt today.
[08:33] [00:13:30] Carlos Mendes: Thank you. We'll send the sample and histogram by Monday.
[08:37] Priya Kapoor: Perfect. I'll put together an initial cost model for baseline + hotpool and a recommended warmpool size based on your traffic.
[08:46] Alex Rivera: Any other questions?
[08:49] Dana Liu: One quick one — do you offer test VPCs for pilot so we can validate egress and network config?
[08:55] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we can provision a test VPC for the pilot period. We'll include instructions.
[09:01] [00:15:00] Samir Patel: Ok that covers it. Thanks all.
[09:05] Alex Rivera: Thanks everyone — next steps recap: deck + SLA (Alex) by EOD, Priya to provide warmpool plan by 6/10, Nexora to share samples by Monday, schedule security review for week of 6/12.
[09:21] End of recording.
